perglm

perglm provides permutation-calibrated, empirically studentized score tests for an exposure in generalized linear models.

Quick start

Supply the nuisance-only null model as the formula, and pass the exposure separately as a numeric vector. The result is a standard R htest object.

library(perglm)

set.seed(42)
dat <- data.frame(z1 = rnorm(120), z2 = rnorm(120),
                  x = rbinom(120, 1, 0.3))
dat$y <- rpois(120, exp(0.3 + 0.2 * dat$z1 - 0.1 * dat$z2 + 0.2 * dat$x))

set.seed(2026)
result <- perglm_test(
  y ~ z1 + z2,
  data = dat,
  exposure = dat$x,
  family = poisson(),
  B = 999L
)
result
result$p.value

The default alternative is "two.sided"; "greater" and "less" refer to the exposure coefficient on the link scale. Set keep_statistics = TRUE to retain the sampled scores in result$permuted_statistics. See ?perglm_test for supported families, assumptions, and fitting controls.

The getting-started vignette walks through this example and its output:

vignette("getting-started", package = "perglm")

Read the rendered getting-started tutorial on the package website. Its R Markdown source is in the source repository.

Development status

Internal helpers fit null GLMs and prepare their working score residuals, weights, and cached projections. Supported families are Gaussian, Bernoulli, Poisson, Gamma, inverse Gaussian, and negative binomial, including fixed offsets. Model observations must be complete, with unit prior weights and a full-rank nuisance design containing an intercept.

Rcpp kernels support scalar and batch studentization, as well as combined exposure residualization and score calculation, alongside an R reference implementation. Three additional internal helpers now provide:

  • glm_score_statistic(): the observed score, with exposure alignment and residual-identifiability checks.
  • permutation_p_value(): inclusive one- or two-sided tail comparisons with the plus-one correction.
  • calibrate_glm_permutation(): fixed-budget label permutation using the cached null fit and bounded Rcpp batches. set.seed() controls the draws; retaining the permuted statistics is optional.

Each shuffle recomputes exposure residuals and empirical score variance. Nonidentifiable exposures and undefined scores stop calibration without a p-value; no draws are discarded or redrawn. The exported perglm_test() function connects null fitting and calibration and returns the test result with null-fit diagnostics.

The package layout includes R code in R/, native code in src/, documentation in man/, tests in tests/, and pkgdown configuration for a future website in docs/.

Reference

Ai, J. and Niu, Z. (2026). Conditional independence testing through marginal permutation. arXiv:2611.03255.
